pronunciation.title: Say it right from day one

rules.explain: a=AH, e=EH, i=EE, o=OH, u=OO. Always. So CASA is KAH-sah.

examples.en: house
table

rules.rule: H is silent, J sounds like H
rules.explain: HOLA is OH-lah (no H sound). J in JUEVES sounds like English H: HWEH-vehs.

examples.en: hello
Thursday

rules.explain: Ñ is like NY in canyon: NIÑO = NEEN-yoh. LL and Y sound like Y in yes.

examples.en: boy
street

rules.explain: Tap your tongue once for R. PERRO (dog) rolls longer than PERO (but).

examples.en: but
dog

rules.explain: Most words stress the middle: HOLA = OH-lah, GRACIAS = GRAH-syahs. An accent mark (á) forces stress there.

examples.en: thanks
coffee

alphabet.title: The Turkish alphabet: 29 letters
alphabet.explain: Turkish uses the Latin alphabet with three letters of its own: Ğ (soft g), İ (capital i with a dot) and Ş (sharp s) — and one vowel most alphabets never meet: ı, the i without a dot.

letters.tip: the i without a dot: arı

counting.title: Counting in Turkish: 0 to 15
counting.explain: Eleven and up is on (ten) + the number: on bir, on iki, on üç.
rules: Vowel harmony: suffixes match the vowels of the word — a back-vowel word gets back-vowel endings.
ı (no dot) and i (dotted) are different vowels: arı (bee) vs arı (carried).
ğ lengthens the vowel before it: çok (very) has a long o.
